Question Choices: Fill: Add the mixed numbers: 4 3/7 + 2 5/7 = __ . (Write your answer as a mixed number)
Hints: Add whole parts and like fractional parts. Regroup any improper fraction, then simplify.
Solution: Add the wholes: 4 + 2 = 6. Add the fractional numerators: 3 + 5 = 8, keeping denominator 7. Regroup 8/7 = 1 1/7; add 1 to the whole part.  In simplest mixed-number form: 7 1/7.

Question Choices: Fill: Add the mixed numbers: 6 2/9 + 5 4/9 = __ . (Write your answer as a mixed number)
Hints: Add whole parts and like fractional parts. Regroup any improper fraction, then simplify.
Solution: Add the wholes: 6 + 5 = 11. Add the fractional numerators: 2 + 4 = 6, keeping denominator 9.  In simplest mixed-number form: 11 2/3.

Question Choices: Subtract mixed numbers: 8 7/10 - 5 3/10. (Write your answer as a mixed number)
Hints: If needed, exchange one whole for denominator-many fractional parts before subtracting. Simplify the fractional part.
Solution: The fractional part is large enough, so no regrouping is needed. Subtract wholes: 8 - 5 = 3. Subtract parts: 7/10 - 3/10 = 4/10. The result is 3 4/10. In simplest mixed-number form: 3 2/5.

Question Choices: Fill: Solve: 14 3/11 - 7 8/11 = __ . (Write your answer as a mixed number)
Hints: If needed, exchange one whole for denominator-many fractional parts before subtracting. Simplify the fractional part.
Solution: Regroup 14 3/11 as 13 14/11 by exchanging one whole for 11/11. Subtract wholes: 13 - 7 = 6. Subtract parts: 14/11 - 8/11 = 6/11. The result is 6 6/11. In simplest mixed-number form: 6 6/11.

Question Choices: Add 3 7/8 + 4 5/8. (Write your answer as a mixed number and simplify)
Hints: Add whole parts and like fractional parts. Regroup any improper fraction, then simplify.
Solution: Add the wholes: 3 + 4 = 7. Add the fractional numerators: 7 + 5 = 12, keeping denominator 8. Regroup 12/8 = 1 4/8; add 1 to the whole part.  In simplest mixed-number form: 8 1/2.
